hints: Focus on the electrons that phosphorus still has left after bonding to three hydrogens in PH3.
Remember that H+ has an empty 1s orbital with no electrons to share, so it can only accept a pair.
Think about what we call a covalent bond when one atom supplies both of the shared electrons to form a new PH4+ ion.
walkthrough:
**Draw the structure of PH3**

Phosphorus is in Group 15, so it has 5 outer electrons. Three are used to form three P-H covalent bonds, leaving one lone pair on P.

Think of it like this:
$$\text{PH}_3 \text{ has a lone pair on P available to donate}$$

**Look at what H+ needs**

A hydrogen ion, $\text{H}^+$, is just a proton with an empty 1s orbital. It has no electrons of its own, but it can accept a pair of electrons to get a stable duplet.

**Join them by sharing the lone pair**

The lone pair on P is donated into the empty orbital on $\text{H}^+$. Both shared electrons come from phosphorus, which is the definition of a dative covalent (coordinate) bond.

Overall reaction:
$$\text{PH}_3 + \text{H}^+ \rightarrow \text{PH}_4^+$$

**Conclude the interaction type**

A new strong P-H covalent bond is formed by donation, not just a weak intermolecular force or electron transfer. So the interaction is a dative covalent bond.

options.A: Correct. The lone pair on phosphorus in PH3 is donated to the empty orbital of H+ to form PH4+. Because both electrons in the new bond come from the same atom (P), this is a dative covalent bond, just like NH3 + H+ to form NH4+.
options.B: Not correct. Dipole-dipole forces are weak intermolecular forces between neutral polar molecules. Here a new strong chemical bond is formed to make PH4+, not just a weak attraction between dipoles.
options.C: Not correct. A hydrogen bond is a weak intermolecular attraction involving H attached to very electronegative N, O or F and a lone pair on another N, O or F. Phosphorus is not electronegative enough, and H+ forms a full covalent bond here, not a hydrogen bond.
options.D: Not correct. An ionic bond involves complete transfer of electrons from metal to non-metal with electrostatic attraction. Here electrons are shared by donation from P to H, forming a covalent bond within the PH4+ ion.
